reviews.text: I played for about 1.5 hours and really enjoyed it. It was fun, the gameplay feels great, and the art is pretty neat. The shield throw skill was my favorite! I always play tanking in MMOs and it feels the developer put a lot of effort and thought of actually mimic the experience of tanking in MMO into a single player. I did run into one bug in the city where I got stuck in a wall and had to restart, which was a bit annoying. The game is also pretty hard, at least for me, but not in a too frustrating way. I lost to the boss several times, one of the hardest. Overall, I enjoyed it and definitely think it’s worth playing.

Ignore the "Early Access" tag for a second; if your idea of a good time is tanking a room of mobs while your healer yells about how their grandma is a better tank than you, this game has exactly for you! Jokes aside, the roguelite loop has definitely kept me entertained. It’s easy to get into and I liked trying different builds between dungeons, switching shields and companions, and going for another run. Notice I didn't mention *clearing* dungeons because the game's challenging and I've yet to find a build that'll carry me through the entire dungeon in record time I’m definitely waiting for the dev to smooth out the set-up phase between runs and make some of the movement skills feel a bit more intuitive, but even in its current state, the foundation is incredibly solid.

There are 3 main issues I saw during my time trying out this game: 1) it's quite rough, 2) it has limited content (even for an EA roguelite) and 3) I think the appeal is super niche. 1) The UI and targeting need work. I couldn't see the health bar of some tall bosses, meaning I couldn't track when taunt would expire on them. The action targeting obviously isn't precise, tab targeting doesn't always select the mob you want, and for traditional targeting there are often too many mobs on screen. The solution is to use the slow-mo function, but that's just a tedious crutch that should neither be present nor needed. 2) One wave attack arena, one dungeon and one boss arena (each with a couple of difficulty levels) really isn't much. I basically did each mode once and was bored. 3) It's an MMO tanking simulator and that already limits the game to an audience that can at least imagine what those words might mean. It isn't even that much like tanking in modern mmos in that it focuses primarily on aggro management, which is less prevalent in modern approaches to tanking. The lack of proximity aggro (on most mobs) is particularly jarring coming from actual mmos. I'm not a main tank, but I have tanked things like M+ and Fellowship and I find tanking in those games way more fun than the "turn red bars into green bars" gameplay here. Boss fights are especially tedious - I get that having to taunt every few seconds is intended to make it challenging by increasing cognitive load, but idk I find it mechanically really uninteresting. Still, this would be a neutral review if that were possible, because the game seems fairly priced for what's there right now.

As a tank main in many games (RIP New World), this game really scratched that itch for me. The mechanics for taunting, kiting, and defending allies are well-implemented. Graphics are good and the game ran well on my lower-end PC. The voice acting for the party members is spot on and downright hilarious. Although the game was fun for an hour or two, the lack of content quickly became apparent. I unlocked and experienced all of the abilities and loadouts within 30 minutes of playing. There are basically only three levels to play. Some game mechanics are not fully explained or frustrating (why is my archer teleporting into a swarm of 10 goblins?). Despite these issues, the game has a lot of potential. I think it just needs another 6-12 months of development before being a really great game.

Neat concept for the genre. Game doesnt have much content atm, but the foundation is there to be GREAT. Once this game gets more classes to play and for your party, more skills, more levels/modes and more enemies this game could absolute rock and become very popular. Ran well and had what seems very little in the bug department from my playtime. Its such a cool concept and hopefully the devs keep watering this plant. Probably a 5$ game in its current form, but this game could grow to be an absolute time killer worth up to 20$ if grown properly.

Although this game is aimed for MMO players looking to tank, as a non-MMO expert I actually enjoyed this game from a different angle - a Vampire Survivors with a twist! It was really refreshing enjoying the high adrenaline of a Vampire Survivors type of game but instead of trying not to die myself, I actually need to protect a companion. Not only that, but I also need to use its help to face enemies better. The concept is really refreshing and as an early access I felt like it had enough play time to get the hook and enough variety of playthroughs without getting bored, but I wish there was a little more skill types and builds as one of the main factors I enjoy in these types of games. All in all, very fun with a great hook and you can enjoy the fun of slaying goblins in a mass not only if your'e an MMO player :)

Review is real 50/50. Huge phat but on this thumbs up. I like the game. I really do. But it just needs a lot of work. It is missing the things that makes tanking good. Things that really show the skill gap between you and the dumb ass DPS players who stand in the fire. Some of the abilities just feel ass. Taunt also seems like it is entirely necessary, and taunt spam is the most boring type of tanking. Chains goes pretty hard when you get upgrades and shield toss is awesome for sure. I'd like to see an AoE slow, leap target the ground instead of just launching you out to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and support for different types of tanking, which is sorta what weapons do. But the difference between like (using Elder Scrolls Online as an example) a warden tank and a dragonknight tank is night and day. One I'm self-healing and buffing, and the other I just gave myself a damage shield and am debuffing. More skill slots with varied builds (maybe a Paladin type tank, a Druid tank, or a Barbarian tank style would be hype down the line) Modes with more party members (leading a full dungeon clear could be fun as hell, bonus points if we can actively tell our dumb ass party mates to go stand somewhere in particular) Pros: Big room mob pulls (what every tank wants to do) Cons: Enemies can be boring. Having more than 2 of the healing foes on any difficult becomes extremely annoying as you just force them to stand on top of each other and use your charge to knock them down and then burst. Targeting could use work. It feels a little bad. A few visual bugs/places you can get stuck if you charge too close to the wall or use the leap.

A Love Letter to MMO Tanking If you've ever spent years holding threat in Azeroth, this game will feel like coming home. It captures that classic pull-and-hold rhythm perfectly, shifting the MMO tanking stress into a satisfying solo roguelite. The talent system is the real hook here—finding synergies that turn you into an unkillable walking fortress is genuinely fun. While the game is currently a bit thin on enemy and map variety, the core mechanical foundation is impressive for a solo dev project. For around $8, it’s a great way to scratch that tanking itch without the monthly subscription or the late-night raid commitment. Check out my full Vibe Check for a deep dive into the classes and mechanics: https://youtu.be/3hLx5Fcjlvc

I recommend this but it's more for what it can become rather than what it currently is. The idea of this is spectacular. Right now though? Once you play it for about 2 hours you've experienced pretty much the entire game and that's if you slowly take your time like me. Having tanked high M+ keys, Savages, Ultimates, etc. this doesn't really feel like any of them in it's current state. The aggro from pulls feels more like a boss with a threat wipe on a 5 second cd so this game is pretty much just spam taunt the entire time. I'm sure that will be fixed in time but for now it quite honestly doesn't really feel good to play. The idea and vision are there but the gameplay isn't. Also it doesn't really feel like you're tanking for anything. Your companion is pretty much just a pet that follows you around to let you use a companion ability. Also they're immobile to the extreme, it doesn't feel good. Right now you just spec all damage, spam taunt, and run through the map. I made it close to level 30 and just felt myself gravitating towards the same few abilities / upgrades that work with zero variation so I'll wait until a new update hits that gives the game something that isn't just taunt being treated as sunder in classic wow. I tanked back then too (Yeah I'm old) and hopefully it doesn't try to follow that route because classic tanking was the most tedious tanking in all of gaming history. Props to the creator of this game though, This game is unique and I mean that in a good way. I hope you make this game into something great, you've already got one foot in the door.

As a Tank enjoyer, I liked this a lot, I feel it does encapsulate the Tanking fantasy very well, and also comes with different game modes. It does feel barebones at the moment, though, but I was already expecting that with the low price and early access tag, hopefully it grows into something great with more content and the current modes more fleshed out.

Great game if you like tanking in MMORPGs, get this game. As a longtime World of Warcraft player of Warrior and Paladin, this felt right at home. Gameplay felt rogue-like which was a great addition. Even for being early access, it's worth the small price. Be warned, it is still quite buggy with shaders and being able to glitch through objects with certain abilities - as of May/June 2026. But even with these bugs, its still a great game and only has room to be even better. My personal recommendation for the developer is to allow people to create builds and save them. I like how grindy the game is for leveling up ( you don't just unlock everything in 2 hours), but definitely could be really cool to build expression and find different ways to play and tank. From being a 2h baddie with no sheild, to a tank that only does thorns and self heals/attricion. I think that could make the game really fun. I love how simple it is, so don't lose that in the process. Progression feels good.

EDIT after additional playtime: After spending more time with the systems, I think my biggest concern is companion flexibility and agency. The Ranger currently feels heavily dependent on a small number of builds and synergies to really shine. If those pieces don't come together, he can end up feeling less like a companion and more like a special ability with legs. I'd love to see him become more active in combat with regular attacks or more autonomous behavior. The Cleric feels stronger overall, but I'd still love to see companions contribute more to the fight instead of mostly existing as triggered abilities. Small attacks, buffs, utility effects, or passive support would go a long way toward making them feel alive. Build variety also feels somewhat restrictive right now. Ranger often feels like it demands specific tank sustain builds, while Cleric pushes you toward specific damage setups. More viable combinations and experimentation would improve replayability considerably. I'd also love to see: Starting abilities separated from gear choices. Larger party sizes so bringing both a healer and ranged companion becomes possible. More companion customization and progression. None of this changes my recommendation. The game is still incredibly fun and the core idea remains one of the best I've seen in years. I simply see the shape of an amazing game here and want more ways to play it.

I feel like it's just currently a small headache / pain in arse with where it is currently in Early Access. But it's still a cool concept of a game just needs a bit of tweaking / balancing. I also believe (if I can recall correctly) when I was also using the protect spell with the +5 hp to companion wasn't working correctly where it wasn't giving them health at all unlike other skills!

Game is fun for my tank heart, however I could do without the timer mechanic. I would love to be able to jump in and take my time tanking on my own without a clock looming. Also the controls could use some polish All in all a fun game I am hopeful for the future of
